mechanism_narrative: A positive month-over-month change in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) directly increases corporate revenue visibility, leading to upward revisions in S&P 500 earnings expectations and positive 20-day forward returns without requiring additional conditions.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS shows positive growth, or the rank correlation between RSAFS growth and 20-day returns is below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that reduces liquidity and increases discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, the S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is above -0.04 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a tightening labor market that drives consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls and PAYEMS rises simultaneously, the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 55% of cases, or the joint signal has a rank IC below 0.04 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an impending slowdown in manufacturing activity that reduces corporate profit growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, a decline in INDPRO is followed by positive 20-day S&P 500 returns in more than 55% of cases, or the rank IC between INDPRO decline and returns is above -0.04 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1300 thousand units, it indicates strong residential construction activity that boosts related sectors and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 1300, the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances, or the rank IC between HOUST and 5-day returns is below 0.04 over a 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) signals persistent inflation that prompts central bank tightening, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises month-over-month, the S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or the rank IC between CPIAUCSL growth and returns is above -0.04 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 4.0%), a further decline in unemployment rate signals an overheating labor market that accelerates inflation and triggers aggressive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 4.0%, a decline in UNRATE is followed by positive 60-day S&P 500 returns in more than 55% of cases, or the rank IC between UNRATE decline and returns is above -0.04 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) and monthly housing starts (HOUST) indicates broad-based economic strength that supports corporate earnings and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 growth and HOUST both increase, the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 55% of cases, or the joint signal has a rank IC below 0.04 over a 3-year rolling window.
